name: The Unimpressed Critic
why_it_works: A snobby, fictional critic sounds like they are about to tear the product apart, so viewers lean in for the takedown. The misdirection flips: every 'complaint' is secretly the highest praise. That surprise makes the compliment funny instead of braggy, which is the only way a brand can brag and still get a laugh.

hook.pattern: Introduce a famously hard-to-please (fictional) critic who just tried your product, framed like bad news.
examples: A very serious critic tried our {{product}}. It did not go well.
We let the harshest critic in town review our {{product}}. Oops.
Bad news. The critic tried the {{product}}.

variables.name: critic_detail
variables.description: One visual detail that makes the fictional critic over-serious
variables.example: a velvet blazer, reading glasses on a chain and a tiny notebook

variables.name: ruined_line
variables.description: The complaint that sounds like a takedown

variables.name: misdirect_reveal
variables.description: The reveal that the complaint is praise
variables.example: I can no longer enjoy any other croissant. My life is worse now.

variables.name: tag_action
variables.description: The critic's small hypocritical action that tags the joke
variables.example: quietly slips a second croissant into the blazer pocket

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer gets for acting

craft.technique: Misdirection: a takedown that turns into praise, with a hypocrisy tag
craft.notes: Setup: bad-news framing and a fictional critic played completely straight, so the audience expects a negative review. Turn: the line that sounds like a takedown ('it ruined me') is followed by the reveal that 'ruined' means nothing else compares; the praise arrives disguised as a complaint. Tag: the critic gives zero stars, then sneaks a second one into their pocket; the action contradicts the words, which is the final laugh. Timing: hold the push-in on the glasses coming off for a full second of silence before the ruined line, and in the tag let the on-screen 'Also:' sit for half a beat before we see the pocket. Never let the critic smile.

do_not: Base the critic on a real, recognizable reviewer, chef or celebrity
Show fake star ratings or review-site logos that could look like real reviews
Let the critic insult other businesses or customers
Use the misdirection for claims you can't support (skincare: no 'fixed my skin' type results)
